newsitem.title: USA: Code-Alarm delisted from National Market.
newsitem.headline: Code-Alarm delisted from National Market.

text.p: Code-Alarm Inc said it has received notification that its common stock will be removed from the Nasdaq National Market, effective April 24.
Code-Alarm said it will continue to trade on the Nasdaq Bulletin Board under the symbol CODL.
The company said it was removed from the National Market because its 1996 year-end net loss caused its net tangible assets to fall below the minimum financial requirements for continued inclusion.

The company recorded a net loss of $7.1 million, or $3.07 per share, on revenues of $62.5 million for the year ended December 31, 1996. The loss was caused by a one-time, pre-tax charge related to the company's decision to divest its European operations and for the impairment of intangible assets for discontinued products.
Code-Alarm manufactures electronic vehicle security devices.
